datasets.data_source: Viechtbauer W (2010). Conducting meta-analyses in R with the metafor package. J Stat Softw 36(3):1-48, doi:10.18637/jss.v036.i03, Figure 1 (p. 15): TB+/TB- counts per arm (Vaccinated = treatment, Control = control). https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v036i03

datasets.title: Introduction to Meta-Analysis worked examples: single-study effect sizes (ch. 4-5), Dataset 1 (Table 14.1, continuous, SMD) and Dataset 2 (Table 14.4, binary, OR)
datasets.data_source: Borenstein M, Hedges LV, Higgins JPT, Rothstein HR (2009). Introduction to Meta-Analysis. Wiley. Chapters 4, 5, 14 and 18; data of Tables 14.1 and 14.4. Data and printed results as given by W. Viechtbauer, 'R Code Corresponding to the Book Introduction to Meta-Analysis by Borenstein et al. (2009)', https://wviechtb.github.io/meta_analysis_books/borenstein2009.html (sections 4, 5, 14 and 18), which reproduces the book's computations with metafor (SMD sampling variances with vtype="LS2", the book's equation; prediction intervals with pi.type="Riley", the book's t(k-2) interval).

datasets.title: Teacher expectancy and pupil IQ: 19 studies, standardized mean differences (Raudenbush 1984), dat.raudenbush1985
datasets.data_source: Raudenbush SW (2009). Analyzing effect sizes: random-effects models. Raudenbush and Bryk 1985, Table 1).
